Workshop 6 · Practice problems

Which words mean the same?

Work these out by hand, without running code, the way the exam works. Total 23 marks. A calculator helps with square roots.

Print

Problems 1 to 3 use these five café orders. A word's neighbours are the word just before it and the word just after it.

1  warm milk please     2  hot milk please     3  warm soup please     4  hot coffee please     5  fresh juice please

Problems 4 to 6 use these sigmoid values:

x −2 −1 −0.5 0 0.5 1 2
σ(x) 0.12 0.27 0.38 0.50 0.62 0.73 0.88
  1. [2]

    Write the neighbour-count vectors of warm, hot and fresh, under the words milk, soup, coffee, juice, in that order.

  2. [3]

    Work out the cosine similarity of warm and hot, and of warm and fresh. Show the dot products and the lengths. warm and hot are never in the same order: why is their cosine not 0?

  3. [3]

    (a) Write the neighbour-count vector of milk under warm, hot, fresh, please, and the same for juice. (b) Work out their cosine. (c) Why is it not 0, and is that a good sign?

  4. [2]

    Word2vec gives the pair (warm, milk) a score of 1 and the pair (warm, juice) a score of −2. (a) What does it guess for each? (b) What does a guess of 0.50 mean?

  5. [4]

    Real pair (warm, milk). The word list of warm is [1, 1], the neighbour list of milk is [1, −1], the rate is 0.5. Work out one nudge: the score, the guess, the error, both new lists, and the new guess.

  6. [3]

    Fake pair (warm, juice). The word list of warm is [0, 1], the neighbour list of juice is [1, 0], the rate is 0.5. Work out one nudge, and say whether the two lists moved towards each other or apart.

  7. [2]

    In a million café orders, warm and hot almost never appear together. Explain, in terms of the nudge, why word2vec still gives them vectors that point the same way.

  8. [2]

    A shop learns product vectors from 2 million shopping baskets, treating each basket as a sentence. (a) What are the "words" and the "neighbours"? (b) Name one thing it can do that a TF-IDF search on product descriptions cannot.

  9. [2]

    A café search uses word vectors to match "cold tea". It returns hot tea near the top. Explain why, and name one other weakness of word vectors.

Answers will be released on the Workshop 6 page after class.
